unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.1 - THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE FUTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will work on and examine the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by searching universal issues in the future, the search for habitable planets, and advancements in space and technology. They will imagine what life could look like in the next century by focusing on how humanity could address challenges such as overpopulation, resource consumption, and environmental crises. Students will research current efforts to discover habitable planets and create a futuristic journal entry. They can enlarge their entry by a model of an advanced technology that could solve a universal issue or expand space exploration. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/ or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school may know what ''universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology'' mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the universe and the future'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as universal issues in the future; search for habitable planets; space and technology'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To describe habitable planets, space exploration, and technology about planets and space in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Creative Writing The teacher provides students with an incomplete paragraph about habitable planets and developments in space technology. For example: ''The search for habitable planets has become the main focus for astronomers and space agencies worldwide. With the launch of advanced satellites and exploration missions, scientists are able to detect potential habitats now beyond our solar system. The development of artificial intelligence and sophisticated navigation systems has made these missions more efficient. However, the challenge is still present such as the resources are limited and environmental conditions are difficult. If humans achieve self-sustaining colonies, __________''. Students work individually or in pairs to complete the paragraph by emphasising creativity and using target vocabulary such as ''civilisation, exploration, radiation, vast, dynamic, potentially''. After completing their work they present their paragraphs to the class. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language with target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space exploration in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Creative Writing The teacher shows some flashcards with visuals representing target vocabulary such as ''rocket, colony, AI, radiation, habitat'' and asks students to match the visuals with the correct words written on the board. When the matching activity is complete students work to complete a worksheet with target grammar in pairs. They use the matched vocabulary to fill in the blanks in sentences such as ''If humans colonise distant planets, civilisations will emerge there'' or ''If we explore the universe, we might discover unknown habitats''. The teacher checks and gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
